scope: Conservative admission for explicit DRW_DxfLegacyExtrusion::toNativeOcs recovery of applied CIRCLE, ARC, TRACE, SOLID, TEXT and INSERT. Existing read modes, legacy applyExtrusion behavior, public model layout, and default writers are unchanged.
authority: Autodesk arbitrary-axis algorithm specifies a unit normal and cross-product axes: https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-E19E5B42-0CC7-4EBA-B29F-5E1D595149EE.htm. Autodesk documents CIRCLE center in OCS: https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-8663262B-222C-414D-B133-4A8506A27C18.htm.
reproduction: Generated CIRCLE normal (1e-170,1e-170,1), native center (0,1e308,0); one legacy applyExtrusion yields WCS (0,1e308,-1e138). Before this change toNativeOcs returned success and native x=1.0000000000000001e-32 instead of zero because a nonzero normal cross-product underflowed before multiplication by the large coordinate. The existing LWPOLYLINE WCS extractor rejects that basis. The source is locally authored, not a committed fixture.
change: Share the existing LWPOLYLINE stable-basis calculation with each explicit recovery helper, invoked only when haveExtrusion is true. Refuse when a nonzero normalized normal or basis component is lost or subnormal, or a checked nonzero cross-product underflows. Copy-before-publication and no-extrusion behavior are retained.

validation.result: 4/4 passed. The six helper types refuse the generated mixed-scale basis with source, destination and aliased input preserved; a no-extrusion control remains writable and corrected nonunit and uniform-subnormal normal retries succeed. ASCII/Binary writer sentinel and same-writer retry controls pass. Existing reader, ARC/CIRCLE, LWPOLYLINE and DIMENSION controls also pass.

limits: This is conservative fail-closed behavior for a known unstable basis, not exact arithmetic or a general guarantee against rounding, intermediate cancellation or overflow. Already lost legacy transformation data cannot be reconstructed. Native 3D rendering and physical-producer profiles are not qualified.
